about: The plain opening of every field note (mission rnd-site-human PR 4, 2026-11-17), rendered after the note’s own header by openNotePages() in scripts/note-openings.mjs (run by scripts/site-sections.mjs) with the lab openings’ renderOpening(). A plain string is words only: no digit and no number word. A number appears only as a quote of the same note’s own words, verbatim, or as a value read from a measured experiment record. plan: true marks a plan whose page holds no result yet. pairs names each written plan (a note or its record) and the note with its result; both notes link the pair, and the build stops when the plan page does not link its result or the result does not link back.

journal/mongodb-ai-ecosystem.html.short: Do the AI tools around a document database give us a reason to replace our relational database? Not yet: each database resumed the tested workflows and returned the same nearest matches from the same embeddings.
found: Saved agent workflows resumed after a crash, but the tool ran again in each recovery; only an operation key in the application kept a duplicate effect from being stored.
Shared thread names and cache contexts led to shared test data, so the application must supply trusted identity scope.
A near question that stated a new policy still got the old allowed answer at score threshold
; adding the new policy and corpus versions to the cache context gave a miss at every tested threshold.
journal/mongodb-ai-ecosystem.html.why: Better AI tooling alone is not a reason to switch databases; start by making sure your application handles retries, tenant identity and changed policies.

journal/mongodb-primitive-fit.html.short: Could a document database earn a bounded role next to our relational database? Not on this evidence: it beat a plain JSON layout in some session tests, but not the stronger relational design, so the relational database stays our default.

journal/why-open-the-floor.html.short: Why show our research work in public while it is still happening? Because the interesting work happens before a launch, and here anyone can read the code, repeat an experiment or report a different result.
found: What we set out: the research subject is the software factory itself, from intent and construction to checking and learning.
What we offer to run: a released tool that checks code against architecture rules people write down, plus small packaged experiments the site reruns on changes, on request and weekly.
What we do not claim: these small experiments do not show that agents become faster, cheaper or more successful.
journal/why-open-the-floor.html.why: You can check our claims yourself by reading the code or repeating an experiment, rather than only reading about them.
journal/why-open-the-floor.html.limit: This is a direction note, not a measured result, and the experiments it points to are small and controlled by us.
